title: Computer generations
competency: Identify the five computer generations and their core technologies.

keywords.def: A period in the development of computers, marked by a major new technology.
An electronic device that controls the flow of electrons in a vacuum; used in first-generation computers.
An electronic device that controls the flow of electricity; used in second-generation computers.
Many small interconnected components on one semiconductor chip; used in third-generation computers.
Very large scale integration: a microchip with hundreds of thousands of transistors; used in fourth-generation computers.
Machines programmed to think like humans and copy their actions; the aim of the fifth generation.
Doing many processing tasks at the same time to work faster.

en.text: A computer generation is a period of development marked by a major new technology. The first generation (1940–1956) used vacuum tubes: huge, very expensive, power-hungry and hot. The second (1956–1963) used transistors. The third (1964–1971) used integrated circuits, many tiny components on one chip.

screens.title: Room-sized computers

opts: They used thousands of large vacuum tubes
screens.after: Vacuum tubes were large and hot, so the machines were room-sized.

table: Vacuum tube: large, very expensive, high power, lots of heat
Transistor (invented 1947, used in computers from the late 1950s)
Integrated circuit (IC) made from semiconductor materials

screens.why: Transistors = second generation; the first used vacuum tubes.

screens.text: Match each generation with its core technology.

screens.ask: The computers that used ___ were called the first generation computers.

screens.text: The transistor was invented in 1947. Why is the second generation dated from 1956, not 1947?
opts: Transistors were not widely used in computers until the late 1950s
screens.ans: Transistors were not widely used in computers until the late 1950s
screens.why: p.3: invented in 1947 "but was not seen widely spread… in computers until the late 1950s". Generations are dated by use, not invention.

en.text: The fourth generation (1971–present) uses very large scale integrated (VLSI) circuits and microprocessors. These made computers powerful, compact, reliable and affordable, and led to the personal computer (PC). The fifth generation (present and beyond) aims at artificial intelligence: machines that learn, using parallel processing to do many tasks at once.

screens.title: A computer in your pocket
screens.ask: Your phone is far more powerful than a room-sized 1950 computer. What made this possible?
opts: Millions of transistors on one tiny chip
screens.after: Very large scale integration puts huge numbers of transistors on a microchip.
